label: Khat (body)
summary: The physical body. Its integrity mattered because other aspects of the person needed a preserved base to return to and be recognised by.

relations.note: One of the aspects the archive treats as a set rather than a single soul.
Mummification and burial address bodily integrity directly.

label: Ib (heart)
summary: The heart as the seat of thought, memory, character, and moral record. It is weighed against the feather of Maat in the judgment scene.

relations.note: Chapter 125 stages the weighing of the heart at the threshold of the hall.
Judgment measures a life against maat rather than against a creed.

label: Ren (name)
summary: The name. Speaking or writing it sustained a person; erasing it threatened memory and continued existence.

relations.note: Naming is an operative act, not only a label.
The attack on Amun's name shows what erasure was believed to do.

label: Shut (shadow)
summary: The shadow, treated as a real aspect of a person with its own mobility and protection needs.

label: Ka
summary: The vital force that continues after death and receives offerings. Khnum fashions the ka along with the body; the mortuary cult feeds it.

relations.note: Offering ritual provisions the ka; the same logic feeds gods and the dead.

label: Ba
summary: The mobile aspect, shown as a human-headed bird. It leaves the tomb, moves between worlds, and returns to the body.

relations.note: The ba's daily departure and return echoes the sun's circuit.

label: Akh
summary: The effective, transfigured state achieved when ritual and knowledge succeed. An akh can act on behalf of, or against, the living.

relations.note: Funerary ritual aims at akh status, not merely at burial.
Letters to the dead address the akh as a party who can intervene.
